title: Neocortical and Hippocampal Theta Oscillations Track Audiovisual Integration and Replay of Speech Memories
description: This dataset comprises raw magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings, T1-weighted anatomical MRI scans, and behavioural logfiles collected during an audiovisual speech memory paradigm. Participants performed encoding, distractor, and retrieval tasks designed to probe theta oscillatory dynamics underlying audiovisual integration and memory replay of speech content. The data support analyses of neocortical and hippocampal theta oscillations reported in an associated Journal of Neuroscience publication.
methods_description: Each experimental block consisted of three successive tasks: encoding (audiovisual synchrony detection to speech movies), distractor (odd/even number judgment), and retrieval (recall and matching of speech stimuli associated with a speaker's face). MEG data were recorded continuously in a single session per participant, split automatically into multiple runs, with associated behavioural responses and trigger codes marking movie onset, visual cue onset, speech stimulus onsets, probe responses, and localiser onsets. Some participants also had individual T1-weighted anatomical scans.
